references.text: The paralyzed man immediately stood up, picked up what he had been lying on, and went home while praising God – this is the immediate context that led to the people's reaction in verse 26.
Here too, the people are seized with fear and awe after a miracle, and they praise God, saying that a great prophet has arisen among them – the same pattern of fear, praise, and wonder.
Fear came upon all who lived nearby after the miraculous events surrounding John's birth – the same reaction of fear (φόβος) at God's works.
Mark's parallel account of the healing of the paralyzed man, where everyone was amazed and praised God, saying, 'We have never seen anything like this' – a direct parallel to Luke's account.
Matthew's parallel account where the crowd was seized with fear and praised God who had given such authority to humans – the same event with the same reaction.

Astonishment (θάμβος) came upon everyone after Jesus drove out an unclean spirit, and they spoke among themselves about what this could be – a similar reaction of wonder and awe following Jesus' miracles.
The people were filled with amazement and astonishment (ἐκστάσεως) over the healing of the paralyzed man at the temple gate – the same word ἔκστασις is used for the people's reaction to a miracle.
The shepherds returned, praising and glorifying God for all they had heard and seen – the same pattern where witnesses to God's works respond with praise.
The disciples were filled with fear and wonder after Jesus calmed the storm and asked each other, 'Who is this?' – a similar reaction of fear and amazement at Jesus' power.
Everyone was struck with awe at God's greatness – the same expression of the people's reverence and wonder at what they had seen Jesus do.
